notes.meaning: God has appointed a set time for every event and action in this world. Life is full of changes, but none of these shifts happen by accident or outside of divine control. People cannot change what God has planned, so we should accept each season with a steady and humble heart.

No one chooses the day of their birth or death; God sets the exact limits of our earthly lives. In the same way, a farmer understands that there is a right season to plant seeds and a right season to pull up crops. Both human life and the natural world move according to the schedule God has established.

There are times when lawful justice or self-defense requires taking life, and other times when medical care brings recovery. Similarly, ruined structures or corrupt systems sometimes have to be pulled down before something better can be built in their place. God determines when an ending is necessary and when rebuilding should begin.

Sadness and happiness take turns in every human journey. Times of disaster call for genuine sorrow and tears, while times of relief and victory call for dancing and celebration. Remembering that hard seasons do not last forever helps believers stay patient in grief.

Clearing stones off a field prepares the ground for planting, while gathering stones together is necessary to build strong walls and homes. In relationships, there are warm seasons for embracing family and friends, and cautious seasons when keeping distance is the wiser choice. Wisdom means understanding which action fits the present moment.

People work hard to earn and find things, but there comes a time when a lost possession must simply be given up. Saving resources for future needs is wise, yet in emergencies, such as a sinking ship in a storm, goods must be thrown away to save human lives. We must never hold earthly things so tightly that we refuse to give them up when duty calls.

In ancient times, people tore their clothing to show deep sorrow and then mended the cloth when the mourning was finished. There are times when quiet patience is best, especially in deep pain or before angry mockers, and times when speaking up for the truth becomes a duty. Good judgment shows us when to remain quiet and when to speak boldly.

Love is a natural blessing, yet there are times when a person must turn away with hatred from evil deeds and betrayal. Nations go through painful wars to protect justice, followed by welcome periods of rest and peace. These shifting conditions remind us that perfect and unending peace belongs only to God's eternal kingdom.

Since all events change under God's control, human effort alone cannot guarantee lasting success. A person may wear themselves out working, yet an unexpected turn of events can quickly undo everything. Real satisfaction cannot come from hard labor unless God provides His blessing.

God has assigned daily work and difficulties to keep human beings occupied. This continuous labor keeps people from becoming proud and reminds us that earth was never designed to be our final resting place. Struggling with our tasks trains us to depend on God through every circumstance.

God makes every event fit into its proper place in His grand design, creating an orderly harmony over time. He has also placed a longing for eternity inside the human heart, so temporal things can never truly satisfy us. Even so, our finite minds cannot grasp all of God's plans from the beginning to the end.

The best approach to life is to be joyful, treat others kindly, and gratefully enjoy our food, drink, and hard work. These simple daily pleasures are not something we secure by our own worry, but are gracious gifts from God. Receiving our daily portion with thanksgiving makes even routine labor a joy.

God's works and purposes are permanent, perfect, and unchangeable. No human power can improve His design by adding to it, nor can anyone spoil it by taking something away. God set up His creation this way so that all people would look to Him with reverent awe and respect.

The cycles of life and nature repeat themselves under God's steady rule, meaning nothing that happens to us is entirely new. God calls back the patterns of the past so that the world runs according to His orderly laws. He will also call every past human deed to an accounting, which reminds us to live honorably.

Even in courthouses where fair treatment ought to prevail, corrupt leaders often bend the rules and harm the innocent. Human power without the fear of God quickly turns into unfairness and cruelty. This shows the painful brokenness of human government in an imperfect world.

Human injustice is not the final outcome, because God has reserved an appointed time to judge everyone. The Lord will re-examine every earthly decision, rescuing the oppressed and punishing wicked leaders. People facing unfair treatment can take comfort knowing that the supreme Judge will make all things right.

God allows injustice and suffering in order to test people and reveal what their hearts are truly like. When powerful men abandon God's ways, they act like predatory beasts toward one another. Seeing our natural weakness helps deflate human arrogance and points us back to God.

When considered only from an earthly viewpoint, humans and animals share the very same physical fate. Both breathe the same air to stay alive, both feel pain, and both must eventually die. Human status and power offer no physical advantage against the finality of bodily death.

The physical bodies of both people and animals were formed from the dust of the ground, and both return to dust when they decay. The grave is the common resting place for all earthly flesh. This sobering fact leaves no reason for anyone to be proud of physical strength or beauty.

While the spirit of a human returns to God for judgment and the spirit of a beast simply dies with its body, physical eyes cannot see this difference. Most people live only for current earthly pleasures and never think about what happens after death. Scripture teaches that human beings have an enduring soul made for God, unlike the animals.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many scholars translate this as "Who knows whether the spirit of man rises upward," reading it as a skeptical question asking whether anyone can prove by observation that humans have a different fate than animals.

notes.meaning: Because earthly life is brief and we cannot see what happens on earth after we die, we should gladly enjoy the work God gives us today. A person cannot return from the grave to manage their possessions or oversee their family. It is wise to live contentedly now with a clear conscience, trusting God with what comes next.
